Control sensitivity audit

Each control was varied separately, keeping wind, reference boat speed and other controls fixed.

Conditions and interpretation

Generic 10 m boat, full main, 105% jib, all controls enabled. Wind at rig head: each knot from 1 to 35. Both tacks. Close hauled 40°, close reach 60°, beam reach 90°, broad reach 120°, deep broad reach 155°, run 180°. Jib at all six headings; A2 at 90/120/155°, S2 at 120/155/180°. Sheets are first moved towards a loaded trim; then a single control is tested at 0, 50 and 100%.

The table shows useful-drive range between the three settings, relative to the highest drive in that sweep. A small range can be correct: an unloaded line or a boom at the shrouds limits its effect. Zero means a response below the numerical tolerance of 10⁻⁷ N. Absent sails are not tested.

12390 responsive sweeps, 0 without a detectable change and 0 without forward drive.

Scope of this check

The CSV contains the three drives in N, their range and a speed-change indicator derived from the cubic law at fixed apparent flow. This indicator is not a settled-speed prediction: the control card instead solves two complete equilibria. This grid does not prove behaviour for every boat, angle or intermediate trim value. Outside tabulated wind speeds, the polar reference uses the educational extrapolations described in the code.

The responses follow the references La barca veloce and La fisica in barca a vela, cited in About. Calculations remain a reduced educational model: they do not validate viscous CFD, a VPP or real performance. Numerical and geometric checks do not replace visual WebGL testing on real devices.
